# Reference Notes 

Made By Abhik Biswas 

**Yes—you’ve got the right idea** , with one important wording tweak so it doesn’t trip you up on an exam: 

You wouldn’t call graphene a _“two-atom basis Bravais lattice”_ (because a Bravais lattice itself is just pure geometric points and doesn’t have atoms or a basis). Instead, the precise statement is: 

## **Graphene is a crystal structure made of a 2D hexagonal Bravais lattice with a two-atom basis.** 

Here is why keeping those two terms separate matters: 

1. **A Bravais lattice** is purely an imaginary grid of mathematical points generated by integer translations **T** = _u_ 1 **a** 1 + _u_ 2 **a** 2 (in 2D), where the surrounding arrangement looks completely identical from every point. In two dimensions, there are only **five Bravais lattices** —one of which is the **hexagonal lattice** ( _|_ **a** 1 _|_ = _|_ **a** 2 _|_ , with an angle of _φ_ = 120<sup>_◦_</sup> between them). 

2. **A Crystal Structure** is what you get when you attach a physical **basis** (one or more atoms) identically to every point of that Bravais lattice: 

Crystal Structure = Bravais Lattice + Basis 

3. **Why graphene needs a two-atom basis** : Because the carbon atoms in graphene’s _sp_<sup>2</sup> honeycomb sit in two alternating orientations (as we saw with the upright and flipped Y bonds), the full set of carbon positions **cannot** form a Bravais lattice on its own. Just like **diamond** (an FCC Bravais lattice with a two-atom basis) or **HCP** (a simple hexagonal Bravais lattice with a two-atom basis), **there is no way to pick a primitive cell in graphene that holds only one atom** . Instead, the primitive translation vectors **a** 1 and **a** 2 of the underlying **2D hexagonal Bravais lattice** connect every _second_ carbon site, and **two carbon atoms** sit inside each primitive cell as the basis. 

## **Quick exam rule of thumb:** 

- **If asked:** _“Is the honeycomb lattice of graphene a Bravais lattice?” →_ **No** (the atom positions don’t all share the same translational surroundings). 

- **If asked:** _“What is the Bravais lattice of graphene?” →_ **2D hexagonal (triangular) Bravais lattice with a two-atom basis** . 

Does that separation between the **Bravais lattice** and the **crystal structure (lattice + basis)** clear up the phrasing? If you’re ready, we can look at how this exact same 2-atom basis idea works in 3D for **diamond** or **HCP** next.
